newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares flat as volume shrinks.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares flat as volume shrinks.

text.p: Russian shares ended flat for the day on Tuesday when the market spiraled down in the afternoon after a brief morning rally that brokers said was built on hopes rather than real demand.

The Russian Trading System index ticked down less than one percent to 165.57 on $13.5 million reported volume. Monday's volume was $16.8 million and last week volumes were in the mid-$20 millions mid-week.
Mosenergo showed a two percent loss for the day, closing at $0.878 after a morning high of $0.906 and Monday's close of $0.894.
Mosenergo accounted for almost $4 million of the trade, while Gazprom, which closed at $0.321 after $0.335 on Monday, showed almost $2 million.
UES, closing at $0.0726 after $0.0740, accounted for $1.7 million and LUKoil, closing at $9.00 after $9.17 showed $1.3 million.
Nick Mokhoff of Alliance-Menatep said the nervous market looked like it would not attract investments soon.
"There is more of a downside to the present market," he said. "There is a better chance of it going down 50 percent on bad news than up 50 percent on good news."
A Western fund manager said the market would not react much while President Boris Yeltsin waited in the hospital.
"The prolonged Yeltsin story will mean a flat market for the next two months," he said.
The market has been slowly gaining ground since September 25, when doctors announced that Yeltsin had a good chance of recovery from heart surgery.

But other rallies in the general market fall since the July 3 presidential election have been short-lived, and although some brokers said new Western funds appeared poised to move the market upward, many said they had seen no significant new funds.
The Monday launch of a Russia index by the International Finance Corporation, widely expected to lift prices, was dismissed as a short term market stimulus by some.
"In the initial stages its not been enough to make a rally in other countries," said the fund manager who expected most new institutional funds to flow in after the new year.
Mokhoff said gas monopoly Gazprom was one of the few bright spots on the horizon.

"The market seems to be falling off, but Gazprom isn't going under 30 cents. It is the good news that everybody is anticipating at the end of the year," he said, referring to a launch of American Depositary Receipts which the market expects by year's end.
